(a) The probability is \int_0^1\int_{1/4}^1 {2 \over 3} (x + 2y) \,dx\,dy = \int_0^1 {2\over3} ({1\over2}x^2 + 2xy)\bigr|^1_{1/4}\,dy = \int_0^1 {2\over3} \left[({1\over2} + 2y) - ({1\over 32} + {\frac{1}{2}}y)\right]\,dy = {2\over3}\int_0^1 (\frac{15}{32} + \frac{3}{2} y) \, dy = {2\over3} \left(\frac{15}{32} y + \frac{3}{4} y^2\right)\bigr|_0^1 = {2\over3} \left(\frac{39}{32}\right) = \frac{13}{16}.
(b) It is easier to calculate the probability that x \lt \frac1{4} + y does not happen, that is, the probability that x \ge \frac1{4} + y, and subtract it from 1. The probability that x \ge \frac1{4} + y is \int_{0}^{3/4}\int_{y+1/4}^{1} {2\over3} (x+2y) \,dx\,dy = \int_{0}^{3/4} (\frac13\,x^2 + \frac43\,xy) \bigr|_{y+(1/4)}^{1} \,dy = \int_{0}^{3/4} \frac13\left(1 - (\frac1{4} + y)^2\right) + \frac43(y)(1 - (\frac1{4} + y)) \,dy = \int_{0}^{3/4} -\frac53\,y^2 + \frac{5}{6} y + \frac{5}{16} \, dy = (-\frac59\,y^3 + \frac{5}{12}\, y^2 + \frac{5}{16}\,y)\bigr|_{0}^{3/4} = \frac{15}{64}. Thus, the probability that x \lt \frac1{4}+y is 1-(\frac{15}{64}) = \frac{49}{64}.
